title: Elleni D
content: I was in the operating room having an appendix surgery. I felt like was out of my dark body, as opposed to my light spiritual body. I looked back to see the monitor that showed my heartbeat as a flat, green line. I stood up from the operating table feeling light, free, and free from pain. The room I was in was divided by a border line. Half of the room was where the doctors were. On the other side there were two of the most beautiful nurses I had ever seen. They were calling my name to come to them. I was going to them, stretching out my hands. My left foot was crossing the boundary line. My other foot was just about to cross the line too. Beyond the nurses was like a garden with fresh air and a beautiful smell. There were many children from different parts of the world, but now they called this place home. They were chanting in front of a man dressed in a gown, but I didn’t see his full face. Most of me wanted to go with them, but a small part was listening to the doctors calling me and telling me not to go. I also wanted to see my sister, who was sitting outside and crying. After much hesitation, I said, "In the name of Jesus, I don’t want to go with you," and ran back to the doctors. After I ran and reached the doctors’ side of the room, I felt as if my ear that had gone deaf was punctured. I heard my heartbeat start from the machine beginning to monitor the "beep, beep." Someone kept waking me by hitting my forehead. I was disappointed because she woke me up. I really wanted to go and thought she stopped me from doing that. When I woke up, I felt severe pain in my chest. The 30-minute surgery took longer than they planned. I heard from my mother that the doctor had told her, "Even though the surgery went well, we lost her. It was tough for us." He said to my mom, "Your faith and prayers have brought her back. It was beyond our control."
